maria (runtime): heads-up: the replay harness numbers for the new kernel-selection change show a reg at p95 TTFT on long-context chat workloads. trying to understand if it's real or an artifact of traffic mix / kv-cache warmup.

devon (perf): can you paste the diffs? is this only replay or also synthetic sim?

maria (runtime): only seen in replay so far. synthetic traffic (our standard poisson+seqlen dist) didn't spike p95. replay shows +18% p95 on 2x8k windows. avg TPOT and goodput look flat.

lee (bench): that smells like kv-cache coldness or different prefix reuse in replay. replay uses real user traces with long tails of repeated prefixes, but also spikes where cache hits drop.

anil (prod-observability): fwiw the deploy bot logs show the kernel pick changed to the "fused-attn-v2" path for those model sizes during the rollout. could be micro-regression under certain seqlen patterns.

maria (runtime): exact log snippet: ```INFO kernel_selector: selected fused-attn-v2 for model=redwood-xxl seqlen=8192 batch=1 est_cycles=1.2e9```

devon (perf): ok. two immediate hypotheses: 1) fused-attn-v2 has higher variance for certain key/value memory access patterns -> p95 hit, 2) batching heuristic interaction: replay bursts compress requests differently than synthetic -> TTFT p95 worse.

lee (bench): to triage quickly: 1) run replay harness forcing old kernel for same trace; 2) run synthetic but with trace-shaped inter-arrival times & prefix distribution; 3) instrument kv cache hit rate and per-request kv latency.

maria (runtime): i'm running (1) now. command: `./harness/replay --trace traces/2025-chat/partition-7.log --kernel "fused-attn-v1" --out run-forced-old.json`

ops-bot: replay job 1720000022 started by maria (runtime) on bench-08. ETA ~12m.

anil (prod-observability): adding metrics to the replay run: please expose these tags -> `kernel=*, kv_hit=true/false, prefix_reuse_bucket, batch_size` so we can p95 by bucket.

devon (perf): quick defs while we wait: TTFT = time-to-first-token measured from request arrival to emission of first token (includes scheduling latency, kernel startup). TPOT = time-per-output-token measured once streaming begins (token emission steady-state). p95/p99 are distribution percentiles over requests for those metrics. QPS counts requests initiated per second; goodput counts useful tokens produced per second (excludes retries/overheads). important: QPS != goodput when batching or caching modifies per-request token cost.

lee (bench): also note that replay harness measures from the original client timestamps, so arrival jitter and client backpressure are preserved. synthetic sim often normalizes jitter -> lower scheduling spikes. that's why apples-to-apples means matching arrival process and prefix reuse.

maria (runtime): replay run finished. initial diff: forcing old kernel removes the p95 TTFT bump. numbers: replay-with-new-kernel p95 TTFT = 124ms, with-old-kernel = 102ms. median unchanged. kv cache hit rate over the high-seq requests was 61% in new-kernel run vs 63% old-kernel (small), but per-request kv latency tails look worse: tail 99th kv-latency went from 0.9ms -> 1.6ms.

devon (perf): that points to kernel codepath adding tail latency on some KV ops. maybe fused-attn-v2 uses a different memory layout triggering occasional page faults or cuda kernel launch patterns. we should profile GPU timelines on a repro run with `nvprof`/nsys.

lee (bench): i'll produce a synthetic run that replays the same arrival timestamps and prefix hashes (so not pure synthetic). command: `./harness/sim --arrivals traces/partition-7.arr --prefixes traces/partition-7.prefix --kernel fused-attn-v2` and compare.

anil (prod-observability): small ask: include a run with kv-cache-warmup=0 vs warmup=1 to see sensitivity. also dump per-batch kernel selection decisions to logs.

maria (runtime): agreed. also let's add a short checklist for root-cause steps so we can close fast: 1) reproduce delta using replay forcing kernels (done) 2) capture GPU timeline + kernel launch latencies on repro 3) instrument per-request queueing time and batch formation stats 4) run sim with trace-shaped arrivals + prefix distribution 5) test kv-cache eviction thresholds and remote memory pressure.

devon (perf): +1. a quick math note for the group: a 18% p95 TTFT reg with steady median usually implies a small subset of requests hitting a tail condition (e.g., rare KV miss path or cold CUDA kernel). if goodput unaffected, throughput likely okay, but user-perceived latency suffers. prioritize fix for production-facing SLAs.

lee (bench): re: apples-to-apples comparisons: we should standardize an experiment manifest that pins: model version, kernel selector config, arrival trace, seed for batching randomness, kv-cache params, and metric windows. then CI can run the manifest and produce a deterministic diff report.

maria (runtime): putting that in a GH issue now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/4521 - will link experiments and artifacts.

ops-bot: link created: https://benchlogs.internal/runs/1720000031 -> artifacts uploaded (repro logs, kv-latency.csv, nsys.tgz).

anil (prod-observability): I'll dashboard p95 TTFT by kernel + prefix_reuse_bucket for last 7 days to see if this is flaky or systematic.

maria (runtime): thanks all. next steps: devon + lee will run GPU timeline + sim; anil will produce dashboards; i'll follow up in the GH issue with links and next actions.

devon (perf): ping me if you want a quick pair debug on nsys traces.

lee (bench): will post synthetic-vs-replay diff summary in GH issue when ready.

maria (runtime): closing the thread here, will reopen if new artifacts show other directions. :thumbsup:
